info.title: LabSentinel API
info.description: Backend for the LabSentinel laboratory equipment monitoring and emergency sample rescue planning system.

schema.title: Response List Equipment Api Equipment Get

post.description: Create a new piece of equipment.

get.description: Retrieve a single piece of equipment, including derived capacity.

patch.description: Partially update a piece of equipment.

delete.description: Delete a piece of equipment (only if it holds no samples).

get.description: List all samples, optionally filtered by equipment.

schema.title: Response List Samples Api Samples Get

post.description: Create a new sample, validating capacity and temperature compatibility.

patch.description: Update or move a sample, re-validating capacity and temperature.

post.description:
Start the temperature simulator.

Idempotent: if the simulator is already running, the existing loop is kept
(no duplicate process is created) and its current status is returned.
Stop the temperature simulator. Safe to call when already stopped.
Enable/disable abnormal (out-of-range) temperatures for an equipment.
Enable/disable a simulated hardware failure for an equipment.

get.description: Return the most recent temperature reading for an equipment.
Return recent temperature readings for an equipment (newest first).

schema.title: Response Reading History Api Simulation Equipment  Equipment Id  History Get

get.description:
Compute the current anomaly risk for a piece of equipment.

By default this is a read-only assessment. Pass ``raise_alert=true`` to
also create or refresh an alert when risk is medium or above.

parameters.name: raise_alert

schema.description: If true, create/update an alert when risk is elevated.
schema.title: Raise Alert

parameters.description: If true, create/update an alert when risk is elevated.

get.description: List active (unresolved) alerts, optionally filtered by equipment.

schema.title: Response Active Alerts Api Detection Alerts Get

get.description: List alert history (resolved and active), newest first.

schema.title: Response Alert History Api Detection Alerts History Get

post.description:
Generate a rescue plan.

Read-only with respect to inventory: this computes and (by default) stores
a *proposal*; it never moves samples. Omit the body to auto-detect unsafe
equipment and use all operational equipment as backups.

get.description: List stored rescue plans, newest first.

schema.title: Response List Rescue Plans Api Rescue Plans Get

get.description: Retrieve a stored rescue plan by id.
List incidents, newest first, with optional filters.

schema.title: Response List Incidents Api Incidents Get

get.description: Retrieve an incident's audit trail (oldest first).

schema.title: Response Incident Events Api Incidents  Incident Id  Events Get

post.description:
Escalate an open or acknowledged incident (-> escalated).

Escalation is an auditable action and does NOT block rescue planning.

Generate (or regenerate) a rescue plan for an incident.

Read-only with respect to inventory. Associates the plan with the incident
and sets its review status to 'planned'. Regenerating supersedes any prior
plan and resets review status.

get.description: Retrieve the rescue plan currently associated with an incident.

post.description:
Approve the incident's rescue plan after revalidation.

Full approval requires a feasible plan; partial plans require
``acknowledge_unrescued=true``. The plan is revalidated against current
inventory and approval is refused if anything changed. Approval never moves
samples or modifies inventory.
Reject the incident's rescue plan. A new plan must then be generated.

Execute an incident's APPROVED rescue plan (simulated sample transfer).

Revalidates the approved assignments against current inventory, then moves
the approved samples atomically in one transaction. On any problem nothing
is moved and a clear error is returned. Does not perform recovery
verification or close the incident.

get.description: Retrieve the execution result for an incident's rescue plan.

post.description:
Record the operator-confirmed recovery outcome after a rescue execution.

``outcome`` must be completed / partial / unresolved. This records only
what the operator confirms and makes no assumption about sample viability.
Requires a recorded execution first.

Close an incident after a recovery outcome has been recorded.

Requires explicit confirmation (`confirm=true`); any unrescued samples must
have been acknowledged during the recovery step. Closure is terminal.

get.description:
Simple health check endpoint.

Returns a static payload indicating the service is running.

EquipmentModeRequest.title: EquipmentModeRequest
EquipmentModeRequest.description:
Toggle an abnormal-temperature or failure condition for an equipment.

``enabled`` turns the condition on (True) or off (False).

EquipmentRead.title: EquipmentRead
EquipmentRead.description: Equipment representation returned to clients, including derived capacity.

EquipmentUpdate.title: EquipmentUpdate
EquipmentUpdate.description: Payload for updating equipment. All fields optional (partial update).

IncidentActionRequest.title: IncidentActionRequest
IncidentActionRequest.description: Optional note supplied when acknowledging or escalating an incident.

IncidentCloseRequest.title: IncidentCloseRequest
IncidentCloseRequest.description: Explicit confirmation required to close an incident.

recovery_recorded.title: Recovery Recorded
recovery_recorded.description:
Backend-authoritative flag: True only when the operator has recorded
a recovery outcome (not 'pending'). Transfer success alone never sets
this - it reflects an explicit operator confirmation.

closed.title: Closed
closed.description: Backend-authoritative flag: True only when the incident is closed.

approval_recorded.title: Approval Recorded
approval_recorded.description:
Backend-authoritative flag: True only when this incident's rescue
plan has a *real, backend-recorded* approval (approved or already
executed, with a recorded review timestamp).

The frontend must use this - not a local/optimistic UI state - to
decide whether an approval actually exists. A frontend-only "simulated
approval" that never reached the backend will leave this False, and the
execute endpoint likewise refuses to run without this backend state.

execution_recorded.title: Execution Recorded
execution_recorded.description:
Backend-authoritative flag: True only when a successful execution is
recorded for this incident (samples actually moved in the database).

IncidentDetail.title: IncidentDetail
IncidentDetail.description: Full incident detail, including affected samples and evidence.

PlanApprovalRequest.title: PlanApprovalRequest
PlanApprovalRequest.description: Options for approving an incident's rescue plan.

PlanRejectionRequest.title: PlanRejectionRequest

RecoveryRequest.title: RecoveryRequest

source_equipment_ids.title: Source Equipment Ids
source_equipment_ids.description: Equipment to evacuate. Omit to auto-detect unsafe equipment.

RescuePlanRequest.title: RescuePlanRequest
RescuePlanRequest.description:
Request to generate a rescue plan.

All fields are optional so the common case ("rescue everything affected by
unsafe equipment, using all other healthy equipment as backups") needs no
body. Explicit lists let a caller scope the plan.

RescuePlanResponse.title: RescuePlanResponse
RescuePlanResponse.description: Structured rescue plan returned to clients.

RescuePlanSummary.title: RescuePlanSummary
RescuePlanSummary.description: Compact row for listing stored plans.

RiskResponse.title: RiskResponse
RiskResponse.description: The current risk assessment for a piece of equipment.

SampleUpdate.title: SampleUpdate
SampleUpdate.description:
Payload for updating a sample. All fields optional (partial update).

Setting ``equipment_id`` moves the sample to a different piece of
equipment (subject to capacity and temperature checks).

SensorReadingRead.title: SensorReadingRead
